title: RF-DETR-S vs YOLOv9-C: benchmark on COCO
dek: YOLOv9-C leads by 2.0 mAP points at 640 px, but RF-DETR-S at 512 px is faster on ONNX, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: YOLOv9-C is the more accurate detector, 57.1 vs 55.1 mAP@50-95 against RF-DETR-S on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch. The resolutions differ: RF-DETR-S runs at 512 px and YOLOv9-C at 640 px, each at its author default, so read this as a deployment comparison. YOLOv9-C is 15.4% faster in PyTorch, 42.3 vs 35.8 FPS, but RF-DETR-S pulls ahead on ONNX Runtime, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5. RF-DETR-S holds a smaller footprint, 176 vs 241 MB peak VRAM.

RF-DETR-S (32.11M parameters, Apache-2.0) and YOLOv9-C (25.5M, MIT) evaluate on COCO val2017 at different input sizes: RF-DETR-S at 512 px, YOLOv9-C at 640 px, each at the author default. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RF-DETR-S and YOLOv9-C highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. YOLOv9-C measures 57.1 mAP@50-95 to RF-DETR-S's 55.1, a 2.0 point gap. YOLOv9-C also leads on small objects: 39.3 vs 35.1 mAP_small, a 10.6% relative gap.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, YOLOv9-C runs 42.3 FPS to RF-DETR-S's 35.8. On ONNX Runtime the order flips, RF-DETR-S reaching 68.5 vs 63.5 FPS. The two are close on TensorRT: 77.5 vs 76.7 FPS on FP32, 71.6 vs 74.7 on FP16.
On edge hardware RF-DETR-S is the faster model. It runs 6.9 FPS to YOLOv9-C's 6.4 on Jetson Orin, and 1.0 vs 0.5 on Raspberry Pi 5.

Pick YOLOv9-C for PyTorch or GPU deployment and for the accuracy edge on small objects. Pick RF-DETR-S for ONNX, Jetson, or Pi targets, where it runs faster at 512 px and holds a smaller VRAM footprint, 176 vs 241 MB. Both ship under permissive licenses.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rfdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRFDETRs.pt")  # 32.11M params, 55.1 mAP@50-95
yolo9 = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLO9c.pt")    # 25.5M params, 57.1 mAP@50-95

results = yolo9("image.jpg")
